passages.excerpt_preview: he study describes Bhagat Singh’s distinctive-hatted portrait as revolutionary propaganda that became a widely recognizable icon of defiant nationalism and imperial injustice.
Its later circulation on posters, stickers and placards shows that visual memory has often detached the image from the complexity of his writing, organizations and political development.
